entries.20:41: Jesus asks the religious leaders a question about the Messiah to make them think. He wants them to reconsider what they actually believe about who the Messiah is.
entries.20:42: Jesus points to a psalm where David speaks of someone greater than himself sitting beside God. This shows that David is not talking about an ordinary descendant but someone far above him.
entries.20:43: This line says that God will defeat all the enemies of this honored figure. It means the Messiah's victory comes from God himself, not from human power.
entries.20:44: Jesus points out the puzzle: if David calls this person Lord, that person must be more than just David's descendant. It means the Messiah is greater than people expected, so we should take him seriously.
entries.20:45: Jesus turns from the crowd to speak directly to his followers while everyone listens. He is about to warn them about a danger they need to avoid.
entries.20:46: Jesus warns his followers not to copy people who show off their religion to get attention and respect. It means we should not use faith as a way to look important to others.
entries.20:47: Jesus says these showy religious people cheat vulnerable widows while pretending to be holy in public. It means God sees through outward religion and will judge those who use it to harm others.
entries.21:1: Jesus watched wealthy people drop their gifts into the temple collection box. It shows him noticing how people give, not just how much.
entries.21:2: A poor widow put in a tiny coin, worth almost nothing. Jesus saw her gift too, even though others would have overlooked her.
entries.21:3: Jesus said the poor widow actually gave more than all the rich people. God measures giving differently from how we do.
entries.21:4: The rich gave from their surplus, but she gave everything she had to live on. Real generosity is measured by what it costs the giver.
entries.21:5: People were admiring the temple's beautiful stones and decorations. They were impressed by outward splendor.
entries.21:6: Jesus warned that the temple would be completely destroyed, stone by stone. Even the most impressive things on earth don't last forever.
entries.21:7: The disciples asked when this would happen and what sign would announce it. They wanted to know the future, just as we often do.
entries.21:8: Jesus warned them not to be fooled by people claiming to be him or saying the end is here. Don't be taken in by confident claims about the end times.
entries.21:9: When you hear of wars and unrest, don't panic, because these things must happen first. Trouble in the world is not a reason to lose your faith.
entries.21:10: Nations and kingdoms will fight against each other. Conflict between peoples is part of the world's brokenness.
entries.21:11: There will be earthquakes, famines, diseases, and frightening signs in the sky. Jesus was honest that hard times are coming.
entries.21:12: Before all that, his followers will be arrested, persecuted, and brought before rulers because of him. Following Jesus can cost you dearly.
entries.21:13: These trials will become an opportunity to tell others about Jesus. Hard situations can become a chance to share your faith.
entries.21:14: Don't worry ahead of time about what to say when you're questioned. Trust God rather than rehearsing defenses.
entries.21:15: Jesus promised to give his followers words and wisdom their opponents can't refute. God supplies what you need when you need it.
entries.21:16: Even family and friends will betray believers, and some will be killed. Faith in Jesus can divide even the closest relationships.
entries.21:17: Everyone will hate his followers because of him. Being loyal to Jesus may make you unpopular.
entries.21:18: Yet not a hair of your head will be lost. God protects his people, even when everything else seems to fall apart.
entries.21:19: By enduring patiently, you will keep your lives. Steady faith through hardship is what saves you.
entries.21:20: When armies surround Jerusalem, you'll know its destruction is near. Jesus gave a clear warning sign so people could act.
entries.21:21: People in Judea should flee to the mountains, and those in the city should get out. When danger comes, don't delay.
entries.21:22: These will be days of punishment when the Scriptures are fulfilled. God's warnings in Scripture will come true.
entries.21:23: Pregnant women and nursing mothers will suffer terribly in those days. Great trouble and judgment will fall on that people.
entries.21:24: Many will be killed or taken captive, and Jerusalem will be trampled by foreign nations until their time is up. God's judgment has limits and a set time.
entries.21:25: There will be strange signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and nations will be terrified by the roaring sea. The whole creation will signal that something huge is happening.
entries.21:26: People will faint from fear as they wait for what's coming, and the heavenly powers will be shaken. Even the strongest will be terrified.
entries.21:27: Then people will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. Jesus will return visibly and unmistakably.
entries.21:28: When these things start happening, stand up and look up, because your rescue is near. Hard times signal that deliverance is close.
entries.21:29: Jesus told a simple story about a fig tree and other trees. He used everyday things to teach a spiritual lesson.
entries.21:30: When the trees sprout leaves, you know summer is coming. You can read the signs in nature.
entries.21:31: In the same way, when you see these events, you know God's kingdom is near. Learn to read the signs of what God is doing.
entries.21:32: This generation will not pass away before all these things happen. Jesus said these events would occur within the lifetime of his hearers.
entries.21:33: Heaven and earth will pass away, but Jesus' words never will. What he says is more permanent than the universe itself.
entries.21:34: Be careful not to let partying, drinking, or life's worries weigh down your heart, or that day will catch you suddenly. Don't let distractions make you unprepared.
entries.21:35: That day will come like a trap on everyone living on earth. No one will escape it.
entries.21:36: Stay alert and pray at all times so you can stand strong and appear before the Son of Man. Prayer keeps you ready for what's coming.
entries.21:37: Jesus taught in the temple each day and spent nights on the Mount of Olives. He had a steady rhythm of teaching and rest.
entries.21:38: People came early each morning to hear him in the temple. His teaching drew crowds who hungered for his words.
entries.22:1: A major Jewish festival was coming up soon. This sets the scene for what happens next, reminding the reader that these events happened during a holy time.
entries.22:2: The religious leaders wanted to kill Jesus but were afraid of how the crowd would react. It shows they were plotting while worried about public opinion.
entries.22:3: Satan influenced Judas, one of Jesus' own twelve close followers, to turn against him. Even someone near to Jesus could be pulled into betrayal.
entries.22:4: Judas went to the religious leaders to arrange a way to hand Jesus over to them. A trusted friend was secretly working against Jesus.
entries.22:5: The leaders were pleased and agreed to pay Judas money for his help. Betrayal was being treated as a business deal.
entries.22:6: Judas agreed to hand Jesus over when no crowd was around. The plan was to do it quietly, away from the people.
entries.22:7: The day arrived when the Passover lamb was killed for the festival meal. This connects Jesus' coming death with the ancient lamb sacrifice.
entries.22:8: Jesus sent Peter and John to prepare the Passover meal for them to share. He gave them a specific job to carry out.
entries.22:9: They asked Jesus where they should get the meal ready. They were ready to follow his instructions but needed direction.
entries.22:10: Jesus told them to follow a man carrying a water jar into a house. He gave them a clear sign so they would find the right place.
entries.22:11: They were to ask the owner where the guest room was so Jesus could eat the Passover with his followers. Jesus had already arranged a place in advance.
entries.22:12: The owner would show them a large, furnished upstairs room, and there they should prepare the meal. Everything was ready for them to use.
entries.22:13: They went and found exactly what Jesus had said, and they prepared the meal. Jesus' words proved true in every detail.
entries.22:14: When the time came, Jesus and his apostles sat down together for the meal. This was an important, planned moment of fellowship.
entries.22:15: Jesus said he had deeply wanted to share this Passover with them before he died. He treasured this last meal with his closest followers.
entries.22:16: Jesus said he would not eat this meal again until it was fulfilled in God's kingdom. He was looking ahead to a future completion of God's plan.
entries.22:17: Jesus took a cup, gave thanks, and told them to share it among themselves. He led them in gratitude and sharing.
entries.22:18: Jesus said he would not drink wine again until God's kingdom came. He pointed forward to a future celebration in God's kingdom.
entries.22:19: Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying it was his body given for them, and told them to do this in remembrance of him. This is the origin of remembering Jesus' sacrifice through bread.
entries.22:20: After the meal, Jesus took another cup and said it was the new covenant made through his blood, poured out for them. His death would establish a new relationship between God and people.
entries.22:21: Jesus said the one who would betray him was sitting right there at the table with him. The betrayer was among his closest companions.
entries.22:22: Jesus would die as God had planned, but woe to the man who betrayed him. God's plan would be fulfilled, yet the betrayer remained responsible for his choice.
entries.22:23: The disciples began to ask each other which of them could possibly do such a thing. They were disturbed and unsure who the betrayer was.
entries.22:24: The disciples started arguing about which of them was the greatest. Even at this solemn moment, they were focused on status.
entries.22:25: Jesus noted that worldly rulers lord their authority over people and are called benefactors. He described how power usually works in the world.
entries.22:26: Jesus told them not to be like that; the greatest among them should act like the youngest, and the leader like a servant. Greatness in his kingdom means serving others.
entries.22:27: Jesus asked who is greater, the one at the table or the one serving, and said he himself was among them as one who serves. He modeled humility and service rather than demanding to be served.
entries.22:28: Jesus acknowledged that they had stayed with him through his trials. He recognized their loyalty during hard times.
entries.22:29: Jesus said he was giving them a kingdom just as his Father had given one to him. He shared his authority and future with those who stayed with him.
entries.22:30: They would eat and drink at his table in his kingdom and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel. He promised them a place of honor and responsibility in his kingdom.
entries.22:31: Jesus warned Simon that Satan had asked to sift him like wheat, meaning to test him severely. Even strong believers can face intense spiritual testing.
entries.22:32: Jesus said he had prayed that Simon's faith would not fail, and told him to strengthen others once he recovered. Jesus prays for his followers, and restored failure can become a source of help for others.
entries.22:33: Peter insisted he was ready to go with Jesus to prison and even to death. He was confident and sincerely devoted.
entries.22:34: Jesus told Peter that before the rooster crowed twice, he would deny knowing Jesus three times. Jesus knew Peter's weakness even before Peter did.
entries.22:35: Jesus reminded them that when he sent them out without money, bag, or shoes, they lacked nothing. God had provided for them when they trusted him.
entries.22:36: Jesus now told them to take a money bag and a sword if needed, even selling a coat to buy one. Times were changing, and they would need to be prepared for danger.
entries.22:37: Jesus said the prophecy that he would be counted among criminals was about to be fulfilled in him. His death among outlaws was part of what Scripture foretold.
entries.22:38: They said they had two swords, and Jesus replied that it was enough. He did not want them to rely on weapons but to understand what was coming.
entries.22:39: Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples followed him. He kept his regular habit of prayer even on this difficult night.
entries.22:40: At the place, Jesus told them to pray that they would not fall into temptation. He urged them to stay alert and depend on God in the face of testing.
entries.22:41: Jesus stepped away from his friends and knelt down to pray. He shows us that even in hard moments, prayer is where we go.
entries.22:42: Jesus honestly asked God to spare him from the suffering ahead, yet he chose to put God's will above his own. It teaches us to pray honestly but to trust God's plan over our comfort.
entries.22:43: God sent an angel to strengthen Jesus during his prayer. God cares for us in our hardest moments and gives us help to keep going.
entries.22:44: Jesus was in such deep agony that his prayer grew more intense and he sweated heavily, like drops of blood. It shows how real his suffering was and how seriously he prayed.
entries.22:45: Jesus got up from praying and found his disciples asleep, worn out by grief. Even close friends can fail us when we need them most.
entries.22:46: Jesus woke his disciples and told them to pray so they would not give in to temptation. We are warned to stay alert and pray rather than be caught off guard.
entries.22:47: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas arrived leading a crowd and came near to greet Jesus with a kiss. Someone close to him used a friendly sign to hand him over.
entries.22:48: Jesus pointed out that Judas was using a kiss, a sign of friendship, to betray him. It shows the pain of betrayal dressed up as affection.
entries.22:49: Jesus' followers saw what was about to happen and asked if they should fight with swords. They wanted to defend him, but they didn't yet understand his way.
entries.22:50: One of the disciples struck the high priest's servant with a sword and cut off his ear. In the heat of the moment, people act rashly and cause harm.
entries.22:51: Jesus told them to stop and then healed the man's ear. Even while being arrested, he chose to heal rather than fight.
entries.22:52: Jesus asked the religious leaders and temple guards why they came after him with weapons like he was a dangerous criminal. He pointed out that their show of force was unnecessary and unfair.
entries.22:53: Jesus reminded them he had taught openly in the temple every day and they didn't arrest him then. He said this was their moment and the time when darkness was allowed to act.
entries.22:54: They arrested Jesus and led him to the high priest's house, and Peter followed from a safe distance. Peter wanted to stay near Jesus but was afraid to be too close.
entries.22:55: A fire was lit in the courtyard, and people sat around it, with Peter joining them. He put himself among strangers where he would soon be tested.
entries.22:56: A servant girl looked closely at Peter in the firelight and said he had been with Jesus. A simple observation put him on the spot.
entries.22:57: Peter denied it, saying he did not know Jesus. Fear made him lie about someone he dearly loved.
entries.22:58: A little later someone else said Peter was one of them, and he denied it again. His fear kept growing, and he kept covering it with lies.
entries.22:59: About an hour later another man insisted Peter had been with Jesus, noting his Galilean accent. The evidence against him was piling up.
entries.22:60: Peter denied it a third time, and right then a rooster crowed. His denial was complete, and the moment of truth had come.
entries.22:61: Jesus turned and looked at Peter, and Peter remembered what Jesus had said about him denying him three times. That look brought everything home to him.
entries.22:62: Peter went outside and cried bitterly. His sorrow shows that he truly loved Jesus, even though he had failed him.
entries.22:63: The men holding Jesus mocked him and beat him. He suffered humiliation and physical pain at the hands of his captors.
entries.22:64: They blindfolded him and mocked him, demanding he guess who hit him. They treated him cruelly and made fun of his claims.
entries.22:65: They said many other insulting things against him. The abuse went on and on, and he endured it without striking back.
entries.22:66: At daybreak the elders, chief priests, and teachers of the law gathered and brought Jesus before their ruling council. His case was now being judged by the highest religious authority.
entries.22:67: They demanded to know if he was the Messiah, and he said that if he told them, they would not believe. He knew their minds were already made up.
entries.22:68: Jesus said that if he asked them questions, they would not answer. He pointed out that they were not really open to the truth.
entries.22:69: Jesus said that from then on he would be seated at the right hand of God's power. He was declaring his authority and his place with God.
entries.22:70: They all asked if he was the Son of God, and he answered that they had said so. He was not backing down from who he claimed to be.
entries.22:71: They concluded they didn't need any more witnesses because they had heard his own words. They used his own statement as their reason to condemn him.
entries.23:1: The religious leaders brought Jesus to Pilate, the Roman governor, because only Rome could carry out a death sentence. It shows how quickly opposition to Jesus turned into an official case against him.
entries.23:2: They accused Jesus of stirring up trouble, refusing taxes, and claiming to be a king, which was a threat to Rome. Their charges twisted his teaching into political crimes to get him condemned.
entries.23:3: Pilate asked Jesus directly if he claimed to be a king. Jesus answered in a way that acknowledged it without playing into their political accusation.
entries.23:4: Pilate examined the case and told the crowd he found nothing deserving death in Jesus. The official judge himself declared Jesus innocent.
entries.23:5: The accusers pushed harder, insisting Jesus had caused unrest all across the region. They kept repeating their claims loudly to pressure Pilate into acting.
entries.23:6: Pilate picked up on the mention of Galilee and asked whether Jesus was from that area. He was looking for a way to pass the case to someone else.
entries.23:7: Since Galilee was under Herod's rule, Pilate sent Jesus to Herod, who happened to be in Jerusalem. Pilate used a legal technicality to avoid making the decision himself.
entries.23:8: Herod was excited to see Jesus because he had heard about him and hoped for a miracle. He wanted entertainment, not truth.
entries.23:9: Herod questioned Jesus at length, but Jesus gave no answer at all. Sometimes silence is the only response to someone who isn't really listening.
entries.23:10: The religious leaders stood there loudly accusing Jesus the whole time. They were determined to see him condemned.
entries.23:11: Herod and his soldiers mocked Jesus and dressed him in a fancy robe as a joke, then sent him back to Pilate. They treated him with contempt rather than taking him seriously.
entries.23:12: Herod and Pilate, who had been enemies, became friends that day over this shared case. Sadly, Jesus' suffering became the thing that brought two rivals together.
entries.23:13: Pilate gathered the religious leaders and the crowd to announce his verdict. He wanted everyone to hear his decision publicly.
entries.23:14: Pilate told them he had investigated their charges and found nothing wrong with Jesus. The judge repeated that the accused was innocent.
entries.23:15: Pilate noted that Herod also found no reason for a death sentence. Two separate rulers had now agreed Jesus had done nothing deserving death.
entries.23:16: Pilate proposed to have Jesus flogged and then released. He tried to satisfy the crowd with a lesser punishment for an innocent man.
entries.23:17: This verse is not included in the earliest manuscripts, so it doesn't appear in many Bibles. It likely described a custom of releasing one prisoner at the feast.
entries.23:18: The whole crowd shouted for Jesus to be killed and for Barabbas to be released instead. They chose a violent criminal over an innocent man.
entries.23:19: Barabbas was in prison for murder during a rebellion in the city. The man they wanted freed was guilty of exactly what they accused Jesus of.
entries.23:20: Pilate spoke to them again because he wanted to release Jesus. He kept trying to avoid the unjust outcome.
entries.23:21: The crowd kept shouting for Jesus to be crucified. They would not accept any other answer.
entries.23:22: Pilate asked a third time what crime Jesus had committed, since he found none. He still hoped to punish Jesus lightly and let him go.
entries.23:23: The crowd kept shouting louder for crucifixion until they wore Pilate down. Loud persistence won out over justice.
entries.23:24: Pilate finally gave in and ordered what the crowd demanded. He chose to please the mob rather than do what was right.
entries.23:25: Pilate released the murderer they asked for and handed Jesus over to be killed. An innocent man died while a guilty one went free.
entries.23:26: The soldiers grabbed Simon from Cyrene, who was just passing by, and forced him to carry the cross behind Jesus. An ordinary bystander got pulled into Jesus' suffering.
entries.23:27: A large crowd followed Jesus, including women who were mourning and weeping for him. Not everyone in the crowd was hostile to him.
entries.23:28: Jesus told the weeping women not to cry for him but for themselves and their children. He was warning them of coming suffering greater than his own.
entries.23:29: Jesus said a time was coming when people would envy those who never had children. The coming disaster would be so severe that childlessness would seem a blessing.
entries.23:30: People would beg the mountains and hills to fall on them to escape their suffering. Jesus was describing a time of terror so great that death would seem preferable.
entries.23:31: Jesus used a picture of green wood and dry wood to say that if this happens to him while things are still relatively good, far worse is coming. His own suffering was a warning of greater judgment ahead.
entries.23:32: Two criminals were led out with Jesus to be executed. He was counted among lawbreakers even though he had done nothing wrong.
entries.23:33: At the place called Golgotha they crucified Jesus between the two criminals. He died in the middle of wrongdoers, exactly as outsiders.
entries.23:34: Jesus asked God to forgive the people killing him because they didn't understand what they were doing. Meanwhile the soldiers gambled for his clothes. He responded to cruelty with mercy.
entries.23:35: The crowd watched while the leaders mocked Jesus, daring him to save himself if he really was God's chosen one. They twisted his power to save others into a taunt.
entries.23:36: The soldiers also mocked Jesus and offered him sour wine. Even his last moments were filled with scorn.
entries.23:37: The soldiers taunted him to save himself if he was really the king of the Jews. They used his identity as a joke against him.
entries.23:38: A sign above Jesus read that he was the King of the Jews. The charge against him was written for all to see, though it spoke a deeper truth.
entries.23:39: One criminal being crucified beside Jesus insulted him and demanded to be rescued. Even in the same suffering, he mocked rather than repented.
entries.23:40: The other criminal rebuked him, asking if he had no fear of God since he was under the same sentence. He recognized that their punishment was just and that something bigger was at stake.
entries.23:41: One of the criminals being executed next to Jesus admits that their punishment is fair, while Jesus has done nothing wrong. It shows an honest man recognizing his own guilt and Jesus' innocence.
entries.23:42: The dying criminal asks Jesus to remember him when Jesus comes into his kingdom. Even at the end, he puts his hope in Jesus.
entries.23:43: Jesus promises the man that he will be with him in paradise that very day. It shows that Jesus offers hope and forgiveness even to someone at the very end of his life.
entries.23:44: Darkness covered the whole land for about three hours in the middle of the day. It signals that something deeply serious and sorrowful was happening.
entries.23:45: The sun stopped shining and the thick curtain in the Temple tore in two from top to bottom. This marked a dramatic moment, suggesting that access to God was being opened up.
entries.23:46: Jesus cries out to his Father, entrusting his spirit into God's hands, and then dies. He faces death with trust in God rather than despair.
entries.23:47: The Roman officer in charge sees how Jesus dies and praises God, saying Jesus was truly a good and innocent man. Even an outsider recognizes Jesus' character.
entries.23:48: The crowd that gathered to watch goes home beating their chests in grief. They leave deeply shaken by what they saw.
entries.23:49: Jesus' friends and the women who followed him from Galilee stand at a distance, watching. They are present but helpless, grieving from afar.
entries.23:50: Joseph of Arimathea is introduced as a respected man who was good and honest. He becomes important because he will care for Jesus' body.
entries.23:51: Joseph had not agreed with the decision to condemn Jesus, and he was waiting for God's kingdom. He was a man of faith who stayed true to his convictions.
entries.23:52: Joseph boldly asks Pilate for permission to take Jesus' body. He risks his position to honor Jesus.
entries.23:53: Joseph takes the body down, wraps it in linen, and lays it in a new tomb cut from rock. Jesus is buried with care in a fresh grave.
entries.23:54: It was the day of preparation, and the Sabbath was about to begin. This explains why the burial had to be done quickly.
entries.23:55: The women who had come with Jesus follow and see where and how his body was laid. They stay close and pay attention, preparing to care for him.
entries.23:56: The women prepare spices and perfumes, then rest on the Sabbath as the law required. They honor God's command even in their grief.
entries.24:1: The women went to Jesus' tomb very early in the morning, carrying spices to prepare his body for burial. It shows their love and devotion to him, even after his death.
entries.24:2: They found the large stone that had sealed the tomb already moved out of the way. Something unexpected had happened before they even arrived.
entries.24:3: They entered the tomb but Jesus' body was gone. The empty tomb is the first sign that something amazing had happened.
entries.24:4: While they were confused about the missing body, two men in bright shining clothes suddenly appeared beside them. This would have been startling and strange.
entries.24:5: The women were frightened and looked down at the ground, and the men asked them why they were looking for someone alive in a place for the dead. It was a gentle challenge to their confusion.
entries.24:6: The men told them Jesus was not there because he had risen from the dead, and reminded them of what Jesus had said while he was still in Galilee. They were being pointed back to Jesus' own words.
entries.24:7: Jesus had predicted that he would be handed over to evil men, killed on a cross, and rise again on the third day. Now that prediction had come true.
entries.24:8: The women suddenly remembered what Jesus had said, and his words made sense to them now. Remembering Jesus' words can help us understand what God is doing.
entries.24:9: The women left the tomb and told the eleven disciples and everyone else with them everything that had happened. They couldn't keep the news to themselves.
entries.24:10: The women who brought the news were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and others with them. These women were the first witnesses to tell the apostles.
entries.24:11: The apostles thought the women's story sounded like nonsense and didn't believe them. Even close followers of Jesus can struggle to believe surprising news.
entries.24:12: Peter got up and ran to the tomb, saw only the linen cloths, and went home amazed at what had happened. Even though he didn't understand yet, he was deeply moved.
entries.24:13: Two of Jesus' followers were walking to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem, on the same day. Life was going on even amid the confusion.
entries.24:14: As they walked, they talked about everything that had just happened. They were trying to make sense of their grief and confusion.
entries.24:15: While they were talking and discussing, Jesus himself came up and walked along with them. Jesus comes near to people even when they don't recognize him.
entries.24:16: Something kept them from recognizing who Jesus was. Sometimes we don't see what's right in front of us.
entries.24:17: Jesus asked them what they were talking about as they walked. He invited them to share their thoughts and feelings.
entries.24:18: Cleopas stopped and looked sad, asking if Jesus was the only visitor in Jerusalem who hadn't heard what had happened. Their grief was obvious.
entries.24:19: Jesus asked what things, and they described Jesus of Nazareth as a prophet powerful in what he did and said before God and all the people. They still respected him greatly.
entries.24:20: They explained how the chief priests and rulers handed Jesus over to be crucified. The religious leaders had rejected him.
entries.24:21: They had hoped Jesus would rescue Israel, but now three days had passed since his death. Their hope had been crushed.
entries.24:22: Some women among them had surprised them by going early to the tomb. Something unexpected had happened that morning.
entries.24:23: The women found the body missing and reported seeing angels who said Jesus was alive. The news was hard to believe.
entries.24:24: Some of their companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they didn't see Jesus. The evidence was confusing.
entries.24:25: Jesus called them foolish and slow to believe what the prophets had said. He gently corrected their lack of faith.
entries.24:26: Jesus explained that the Messiah had to suffer these things before entering his glory. Suffering was part of God's plan, not a failure.
entries.24:27: Starting with Moses and all the prophets, Jesus explained what the Scriptures said about himself. The whole Bible points to Jesus.
entries.24:28: As they approached Emmaus, Jesus acted as if he would keep going. He didn't force himself on them.
entries.24:29: They urged him to stay because it was getting late, and he went in with them. They wanted more of his company.
entries.24:30: When they sat down to eat, Jesus took the bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them. This simple act became the moment of revelation.
entries.24:31: Suddenly they recognized who he was, and then he disappeared from their sight. Recognition came, but so did his departure.
entries.24:32: They said to each other that their hearts had been burning while he talked with them and explained the Scriptures. God's word had stirred them deeply.
entries.24:33: They got up right away and returned to Jerusalem, where the eleven and others had gathered. They couldn't wait to share the news.
entries.24:34: They told the group that the Lord had truly risen and that Simon Peter had seen him. The resurrection was being confirmed by multiple witnesses.
entries.24:35: They told how they had recognized Jesus when he broke the bread. Their story added to the growing evidence.
entries.24:36: While they were still talking, Jesus himself stood among them and said, Peace be with you. He greeted them with calm and reassurance.
entries.24:37: They were terrified and thought they were seeing a ghost. Fear was their first reaction to the supernatural.
entries.24:38: Jesus asked why they were upset and doubting. He addressed their fear directly and gently.
entries.24:39: He invited them to look at his hands and feet and touch him, showing he had a real body, not a spirit. He wanted them to know he was truly alive.
entries.24:40: After saying this, he showed them his hands and feet. He gave them physical proof of his resurrection.
entries.24:41: The disciples were so happy and amazed that they still couldn't quite believe it was really Jesus. So he asked them for something to eat to show them he was truly alive and real.
entries.24:42: They handed him a piece of cooked fish. It was a simple, ordinary thing, but it proved he had a real body they could touch and see.
entries.24:43: He ate the food right in front of them. This showed them plainly that he was not a ghost or a vision but the same Jesus they had known.
entries.24:44: Jesus reminded them that he had told them all this would happen while he was still with them. He explained that everything written about him long ago in the Scriptures had to come true.
entries.24:45: Then he helped them understand what the Scriptures actually meant. What had been confusing or hidden to them before now made sense.
entries.24:46: He told them the Scriptures said the Messiah had to die and then rise from the dead on the third day. This was God's plan all along, not a tragic accident.
entries.24:47: He said the message of turning back to God and being forgiven must be preached, starting in Jerusalem and then going out to every nation. This good news is for all people everywhere, including you.
entries.24:48: He told his followers that they had seen these things with their own eyes and were now witnesses to tell others. If you know what Jesus has done, you too have something to pass on.
entries.24:49: He promised to send them what the Father had promised, a power from heaven. But they had to stay in the city and wait for it rather than rush off on their own.
entries.24:50: He led them out toward Bethany and raised his hands to bless them. Even as he was leaving, he was giving them something good.
entries.24:51: While he was blessing them, he left them and was carried up into heaven. His departure was peaceful and full of blessing, not a sad goodbye.
entries.24:52: They worshiped him and went back to Jerusalem full of great joy. Their sorrow turned into gladness because they knew he was alive and still with them in spirit.
entries.24:53: They spent their time in the Temple praising God. Their joy and gratitude showed in how they worshiped, and that is a natural response to knowing what God has done.
